content: 1. Both aripiprazole and rilpivirine can prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of arsenic trioxide by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 3. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 4. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of artemether/lumefantrine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 5. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of asenapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 6. Both asenapine transdermal and rilpivirine can prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 7. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 8. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine may significantly decrease rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. If antacids must be administered, they should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours afterward. 9. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 10. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 11. Both atomoxetine and rilpivirine can prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 12. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 13. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 14. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of chlorpromazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 20. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance due to decreased levels. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 21. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 22. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of citalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 23. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 27. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 28. Crizotinib increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 29. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of cyclobenzaprine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 30. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dasatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 31. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of desipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 33. Both deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine can prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain circumstances, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QTc-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation, may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes and/or sudden death. 34. Didanosine affects rilpivirine metabolism via hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. This interaction applies to didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution powder. Administer rilpivirine at least 2 hours before or several hours after didanosine. No dose adjustment is required when rilpivirine is co-administered with didanosine. Didanosine should be taken on an empty stomach, at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine, which should be taken with a meal. 35.
